title: Nut and bolt
prompt: A labelled teaching adaptation of pages 62 and 64 uses a nut and bolt through clearance holes in two metal plates. An external hand restrains the bolt head. Tighten turns the nut with a spanner, draws it toward the head and clamps the plate stack. Loosen reverses the nut and releases the clamp. Pull applies a modest external separating load while the tightened joint remains intact. See-through exposes the mating thread flanks, head and nut bearing faces and plate holes. Overlays distinguish bolt tension from plate compression. The plate stack and test load are teaching fixtures. Do not thread both plates or claim unlimited holding force.
chapter: Part 1: The Mechanics of Movement / Screws
blurb: A teaching adaptation of pages 62 and 64 follows preload through a restrained bolt, mating nut and two clearance-hole plates.
fixtures: Two metal plates with clearance holes
truthNotes: Manufactured mating threads clamp unthreaded plates.
Bolt head remains restrained while nut and spanner turn together.
Enlarged geometry, slowed motion and exaggerated elastic displacement.
Illustrative elastic model uses 1000 N preload and a 100 N test load. It is not a strength rating.
Pull is available only after tightening. Friction holds the nut at rest.
Cutaway appears only in see-through mode.
This is an accepted teaching application, not a literal reproduction of the page 64 drawing.
